subject: Recap & Next Steps — inference length buckets, token mix & budget target
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
To: Ellen Ramirez <ellen@retaillytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & Next Steps — inference length buckets, token mix & budget target

Hi Ellen / Tom —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and the pieces we promised to follow up on related to context length and costing: 

Summary of what you shared (high-level):
- Production use: customer support summarization + conversational help across web + mobile.
- Expected traffic: 120M completions per month in Q1 (spikey weekdays).
- Current unit target: internal leadership is aiming for ~ $1,000–$1,500 per 1M tokens as a ballpark for total inference (prompt + completion) — we discussed improving economics via batching & caching.
- Context needs: ~70% of requests are short (<= 2k tokens total), ~25% require 8k windows for long session history, and ~5% are multi-document retrievals where you foresee a potential need for 32k or 128k in limited experiments.

Data points we captured for pricing profiling:
- Avg prompt tokens (sampled from your dataset): 320 tokens
- Avg completion tokens: 420 tokens
- Median conversation depth: 4 turns (prefix cache opportunity)
- Long-call tail: 90th percentile completion ~ 3,800 tokens (these are the ones that drive 32k / 128k decisions)

Next steps (agreed):
1) I will send a cleaned usage sample and an initial pricing estimate that shows per-1M unit economics for three offering configurations (hosted standard, dedicated reserved baseline, and burst-capable dedicated). Attachment: retaillytics_usage_sample.csv + redwood-pricing-estimate-v2.xlsx
2) You’ll validate the sample against anonymized production logs and flag any differences in token mix / long-tail frequency.
3) If the long-tail (32k/128k) experiments are material after you validate, we’ll run a 30-day pilot that isolates those flows so we can show real per-token costs and latency trade-offs.

A few clarifications we need from your side to finalize the estimate:
- Exact expected sustained QPS during peak hour (or a conservative peak multiplier).
- Any hard cap on $/1M you want us to use for the internal approval path (you mentioned $1,000–$1,500).

Proposed short-term ask: can you confirm whether leadership would accept an initial committed price target of $1,250 / 1M tokens for a Dedicated baseline with a 6-12 month commit? That lets us dimension reserved capacity and offer the lowest unit.

I’ll follow up with the estimate in a separate email (attached). Thanks again for the time — will be standing by for the log sample validation.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: retaillytics_usage_sample.csv (CSV, 84KB)]
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimate-v2.xlsx (XLSX, 96KB)]

From: Ellen Ramirez <ellen@retaillytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Cho <tom.cho@retaillytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & Next Steps — inference length buckets, token mix & budget target

Thanks Vanessa — helpful summary. Couple quick notes from our side after an internal sync: 

- Peak QPS: current prod baseline is ~35 qps, but marketing promotions push a ~3x spike for 2–3 hours/day. For budgeting assume 100 qps sustained at peak.
- Token mix validation: we ran the sample across last 30 days and the avg prompt/completion numbers look right (320 / 420) — I’m attaching a short extract we generated for you.
- On the $/1M: leadership wants us to start negotiation at $1,200 / 1M for Dedicated with a 12-month commitment; they want clear gating criteria to drop to $1,000 if we hit a usage threshold after month 3.

Two asks:
1) Can you show a worked example of how caching + batching could get us from the raw per-token math to your committed-dollar target? A simple table that maps token mix to effective $/1M after those mitigations would be great.
2) We’d like a separate row in the estimate for a scenario where 8k windows are default (not just tail) — that would cover agent context retention for complex tickets.

Will send the extract in a follow-up.

— Ellen

[Attachment: retaillytics_sample_extract.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
To: Ellen Ramirez <ellen@retaillytics.com>, Tom Cho <tom.cho@retaillytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 06 Dec 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & Next Steps — inference length buckets, token mix & budget target

Ellen — thanks for the quick validation and the spike numbers, that’s super helpful. I’ve updated the estimate worksheet (attached) and pulled a short worked example below to illustrate how batching + prefix caching affect effective cost.

Worked example (illustrative):
- Raw token mix (monthly): prompts 38M tokens, completions 50M tokens = 88M total tokens
- Raw unit price (hosted model list) baseline: $1,800 / 1M tokens (unoptimized) -> raw spend = $158,400/month
- With Redwood Dedicated + batching: we model a 22% reduction in effective tokens via batching (amortized prompt overhead) -> effective tokens = 68.6M
- With prefix KV caching applied to sessions (75% of user journeys): additional 12% effective reduction -> effective tokens = 60.4M
- Effective blended unit price offered for a 12-month committed Dedicated config in the attached sheet: $1,250 / 1M tokens -> effective monthly cost = $75,500 (illustrative)

Notes on length buckets:
- If 8k becomes the default for 25% of traffic, we show two rows: baseline (8k-lite where KV cache keeps average token window small) and 8k-default (no cache for some flows). The 8k-default scenario raises effective tokens by ~18% vs baseline in our model.
- For the 5% of experimental flows that need 32k/128k, we recommend isolating them into a pilot pool so you only pay premium pricing for that small slice — this keeps the blended $/1M lower for the majority of traffic.

Proposed next steps:
- Internal redwood action: Karthik to run a cost-sensitivity model that maps your spike multiplier (1x, 2x, 3x) to required reserved GPU counts and the resulting per-1M price bands.
- Retaillytics action: confirm if leadership is OK to start negotiation at $1,200 / 1M with the gating clause you suggested; if yes we’ll produce a 1-page term sheet for legal to review.

I’ll ask Karthik to attach the sensitivity outputs later today. If you’re comfortable we can lock a short call next week to review the term sheet and sizing (30 minutes).

Thanks —
Vanessa

[Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimate-v2.xlsx (XLSX, updated 06 Dec 2026)]

From: Tom Cho <tom.cho@retaillytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ellen Ramirez <ellen@retaillytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Recap & Next Steps — inference length buckets, token mix & budget target

Thanks Vanessa — that example helps a lot. Quick confirmation from our side:

- We’re OK to start at $1,200 / 1M for the 12-month committed Dedicated baseline with the gating clause to revisit to $1,000 if we pass a 3-month usage threshold.
- We like the pilot approach for 32k/128k flows — please include estimated latency uplift and any minimums in the pilot terms.

Let’s do 30 minutes next Tue (Dec 14) at 10am PT to walk the term sheet and the sensitivity model. Ellen will send an invite.

— Tom
